newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investor dumps PaineWebber.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investor dumps PaineWebber.

text.p: An investor exited a big position in options on shares of PaineWebber Group Inc less than two weeks after opening it, traders said Friday.
The PaineWebber January 25 call traded 11,973 contracts, most of which was done in two blocks, one of 7,463 and one of 2,500. The option had open interest of about 9,100.
Traders said exiting such a long-dated position after only two weeks was strange, and they were unsure of the strategy behind the unwinding.
"He came in today and bought the calls back and sold the stock and did it delta neutral," a trader said.
A delta neutral trade offsets positive and negative deltas. Delta is the change in an option price for a given change in the underlying security's price.
The trader said the calls were bought at 1-1/16 and the stock sold at 23-3/8 and that the delta was 36.
"It was just unwinding a position," the trader said. "We couldn't get any information as to why or what was going on. It was just what he wanted to do."
In other trading, U.S. Robotics Corp options were busy as the stock fell for a second straight session.
The stock, which lost nearly four points on Thursday, closed down 2-7/8 at 60 Friday. Turnover was heavy at 6.3 million shares.
"We continue to see an enormous expansion in volatility in U.S. Robotics" options, said Andrew Schwarz, senior partner at AGS Specialist Partners.
"There's a lot of speculation in the earnings, a lot of speculation in new products," he said. "The speculation is leading to" the increase in volatility.
The company is expected to report earnings on November 4.
Schwarz said most of the rise was on the call side.
On the American Stock Exchange, the most active U.S. Robotics options included the November 65 call and the November 70 call.
The November 65, which traded 1,415 contracts, fell 1-1/8 to 2-5/8. The November 70 fell 3/4 to 1-3/8. It traded 1,280 contracts.
On the Chicago Board Options Exchange, the November 75 call traded 2,679 contracts and ended at 3/4, down 5/16.
